faq.a: Lower quality means a smaller file but more visible artifacts. Quality 80 is a good balance for photos; use higher values when detail matters.
faq.q: What quality setting should I use?

faq.a: The tool outputs JPEG (or PNG if the original has transparency and you keep PNG). JPEG is much smaller for photos.
faq.q: What format does the compressed image use?

faq.a: No. The file is read and processed entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
